The internet is used only for this: LockTime asks GitHub for the latest version number and, if you tap “Update”, downloads it. Nothing about you, your apps or your usage is sent. Turn it off and LockTime makes no network requests at all.
Update checks are off — LockTime doesn’t go online.
Couldn’t check. Check your connection and try again.
Download failed. Try again or open the release page.

To check for updates, LockTime needs the internet. Here’s exactly what happens:

• Once a day when you open Settings, and when you tap “Check now”, LockTime asks GitHub (where its code lives) for the number of the latest version.
• If you tap “Update”, it downloads the new version from GitHub.

What is NOT sent: your apps, usage time, limits or any settings. GitHub only sees an ordinary request, like opening any website.

You can change this anytime: Settings → Updates.

To install the update, Android needs you to allow “Install unknown apps” for LockTime. The page will be in the phone’s language — turn the switch on (“Allow from this source”), come back and tap “Update” again.
